{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"On a windy Saturday, Leo discovered a brass key tucked beneath a loose floorboard in the attic. It was old and heavy, with a tiny star engraved on its handle. He carried it downstairs, where his aunt was sorting boxes of family photographs.

“Do you know what this opens?” he asked.

His aunt turned the key over in her palm. “Perhaps the cabinet in the garden shed,” she said. “Your great-grandmother kept her gardening tools there.”

The shed stood behind the house, almost hidden by climbing ivy. Its wooden door groaned when Leo pushed it open. Inside, pots and rakes leaned against the walls, and a dusty green cabinet sat in the corner. The key slipped into its lock and turned with a satisfying click.

The cabinet held no tools. Instead, it contained packets of seeds, a pair of worn gloves, and a notebook filled with handwritten notes. Leo opened it carefully. His great-grandmother had recorded when she planted each flower and what the garden looked like through the seasons. On the last page, she had drawn a simple map of the yard, marking a small bed beside the fence.

Leo and his aunt found the bed beneath a tangle of weeds. They cleared the soil and planted the seeds they discovered in the cabinet. As they worked, his aunt shared stories of helping her grandmother there as a child.

Weeks later, the first green shoots appeared. By summer, bright yellow flowers nodded beside the fence. Leo added a new page to the notebook, sketching the garden as it looked now. Beneath the drawing, he wrote: “Some keys open doors. Others help old stories grow again.”"}
